content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim in the document against the evidence, starting with the root cause, which rests on F1 and is hedged as unverified. For the plain-words explanation, the question is whether "anyone who hasn't bought anything this month" also covers shoppers with no purchase history at all, since F1 seems to describe only those who bought earlier.

I'm verifying the remaining claims against the logs: the flag was still evaluating on after the switch-off, and the same ZeroDivisionError kept firing in those minutes, which matches the error level the Mitigation Agent saw. The account-page error rate also clearly jumped, from about 0.9 to 19.1.

I'm checking whether the causal chain holds: the logs show the flag evaluating on for account page requests in the same minutes the ZeroDivisionError fired, and that co-occurrence, along with the code path, supports the claim. I'll accept it as supported.

I'm checking the ruled-out claims against the flag history, where only one change by anyone other than Argus shows up in the hour before each check, and that is the same P1 switch-on. I'm also confirming the causal chain's last link, which cites F1 as its source.

I'm checking the second claim in the flag-history section, that most account page evaluations in the first minute already read the flag as on, against the logged counts for that minute.

I'm checking the remaining claims against the logs: the flag still logged as on after the switch-off, the ZeroDivisionError kept firing in those same minutes, and the alert fired later than expected. I'm also confirming that the mitigation was judged refuted and switched back on, and that the error only showed up in the minutes when the flag was still being read as on.

I'm checking the mitigation record now: the switch-back was judged on logs read before 03:29:16, so nothing from after that point was examined. I'm also confirming that Argus treated the earlier switch-off as the full test of the second claim, even though that claim described the errors tracking the flag's evaluations minute by minute.

I'm checking the last few lines of the document, which are only recommendations, so there's nothing new to verify there.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out the shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing this month's total by the number of purchases made this month, in `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Nothing guards against an empty month, so a shopper who has bought before but not this month raises ZeroDivisionError and their account page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching on a new monthly spending summary on account pages sent shoppers into a calculation that likely divides by the number of things they bought this month, and that fails for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month.
With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for any shopper who has bought before but not this month.
After the switch-off the service still logged the flag evaluating on in {Gce95.5}, and ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes ({G5309.4}).
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's error rate across all its requests rose far above its usual level.
rows: The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9%
The same rate while it was broken: 19.1%

supported.quote: Account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error was logged from the minute of onset onward, while before it account pages were logged rendering normally.

The requests reaching that code were the ones that evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on. Admin switched the flag on at {P1.1}, and from that minute the service logged it evaluating on for account page requests, alongside the errors.

A deploy or other code change setting it off: the change events read back only the flag changes, all replicas ran the same revision, and account pages were logged rendering normally up to the minute before the flag was switched on.
Another flag change: apart from this one, the flag provider's history showed no flag change by anyone but Argus.
With the flag on, the account page divides this month's spend by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
No test or check was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production.
The flag was not seen being rolled out in stages, and no automatic halt on rising errors was seen. In the minute it was switched on, most logged account page evaluations already read it as on.
The ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was paged.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: The alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval, scraping allowance and onset minute account for. The record does not show what took the rest.
rows: The alert came 3 minutes 36 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for

supported.quote: The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and switched monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet after the switch-off, ZeroDivisionError was logged only in the minutes when the flag was still logged evaluating on ({G5309.4} and {Gce95.5}). Switching it back on likely let more account page requests evaluate it as on and reach the failing path. No log from after it was put back on was read.
Argus counted C2 as already tested by the switch-off and moved to FIXING with nothing further to try. But C2 said the errors followed the flag's evaluations minute by minute
